case.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit
case.limits: Section 512 protects storage at a user's direction. A provider that generates the material itself is not obviously storing anything at anyone's direction.
case.holding: The section 512(c) safe harbour requires knowledge of specific infringing material, not a general awareness that infringement occurs on a service.

case.why_ai_cites_it: The template for platform-layer defenses now raised by model hosts and AI marketplaces: liability attaches to what you were told about specific material, not to what you could have guessed about your users in general.

reading.body:
The knowledge standard established in *Viacom v. YouTube* is the primary shield AI companies now invoke when sued over content their systems processed or reproduced: liability requires awareness of specific infringing material, not a general sense that infringement probably occurs.

The Second Circuit held in 2012 that Section 512(c) of the DMCA protects storage of material at a user's direction, and that a platform loses that protection only when it has knowledge of particular infringing items, not when it merely has reason to suspect its users infringe broadly. That distinction, specific versus general knowledge, is precisely what model hosts and AI marketplaces argue when plaintiffs claim they should have known their training data or user-generated outputs contained protected works. The data lists eight live cases against AI companies that cite this precedent, out of 79 active cases total, which suggests the defense is already in routine use rather than being tested at the edges.

The data also records a limit the courts have not yet resolved. Section 512(c) covers storage at a user's direction. A model that generates material itself, rather than storing something a user uploaded, is not straightforwardly within that language. Whether the safe harbour extends to generative output rather than stored content is the open question this precedent leaves, and the live cases listed here are among the forums where that question is being pressed.
